column3: RFC 5861 SS3/SS3.1: caches MAY serve stale up to the indicated seconds; SS3.1 example max-age=600 + swr=30, staleness 15 inside window.
RFC 5861 SS3.1 "up to an additional 30 seconds" + SS4 "more stale than the indicated amount" SHOULD NOT: staleness 30 is not more stale than 30, boundary inclusive.
RFC 5861 SS3: if delta-seconds passes without revalidation, response SHOULD NOT continue to be served stale.
RFC 9111 SS4.2: response_is_fresh = (freshness_lifetime > current_age); 599 < 600 -> fresh.
RFC 9111 SS4.2 formula: 600 > 600 false -> stale; RFC 5861 SS3 window covers staleness 0 <= 30.
RFC 5861 SS4.1 example verbatim: age 900 (stale 300 of 1200) usable on 500.
RFC 5861 SS4.1: usable until age greater than 1800; exactly 1800 still within stale-if-error=1200.
RFC 5861 SS4.1: after age greater than 1800 the cache must write the error message through.
RFC 5861 SS4: an error is any situation that would result in 500/502/503/504.
RFC 5861 SS4: 503 in the enumerated set.
RFC 5861 SS4: 504 in the enumerated set.
RFC 5861 SS1 ("a network segment, or DNS failure") + SS4: network failure maps to the error class; contract input string "network".
RFC 5861 SS4: 404 outside the enumerated set -> not-an-error.
RFC 5861 SS4: 501 not in the enumerated set.
RFC 5861 SS4: 429 not in the enumerated set.

RFC 5861 SS1 "two independent" extensions: SS3 governs serving while revalidating, SS4 governs error serving; no sie present and 9111 SS4.2.4 forbids stale generation absent permission -> error-through. Interpretive gap noted as contract finding F1.
RFC 5861 SS4: stale-if-error applies when an error is encountered; plain request past freshness with no swr -> revalidate (9111 SS4.2.4).

Contract Decision rule 4 lane convention (request stale-if-error takes precedence when present); RFC 5861 SS4 gives request scope its own application but does not fix precedence over the response directive.
Contract Decision rule 4 lane convention (request-first precedence); RFC 5861 SS4 silent on request/response overlap.
RFC 5861 SS4: "when used as a request Cache-Control extension, its scope of application is the request it appears in" - request-only sie serves stale on error.
RFC 9111 SS5.2.2.2: "in all circumstances, a cache MUST NOT ignore the must-revalidate directive"; disconnected cache MUST generate error rather than reuse stale; overrides 5861 SS4 MAY.
RFC 9111 SS5.2.2.2 + SS4.2.4 prohibition list: stale generation prohibited by must-revalidate.
RFC 9111 SS5.2.2.4: response MUST NOT be used without successful validation, fresh or not (9111 SS4 reuse list).
RFC 9111 SS5.2.2.4: even caches configured to send stale responses must not; error-through.
RFC 9111 SS5.2.1.4 client preference implemented as prohibition (contract choice; request directives advisory per SS5.2.1 intro - contract finding F2).
RFC 9111 SS5.2.2.8: shared cache MUST NOT reuse stale response until successfully validated.
RFC 9111 SS5.2.2.8: "proxy-revalidate does not apply to private caches" (shared=false).
RFC 9111 SS5.2.2.10: shared cache MUST NOT reuse a stale response with s-maxage until validated; A=900 >= L=600 so genuinely stale.
RFC 9111 SS5.2.2.10: s-maxage applies to shared caches only; shared=false -> prohibition inapplicable.
RFC 5861 SS3 ABNF stale-while-revalidate = delta-seconds; 9111 SS1.2.2 delta-seconds = 1*DIGIT, SS5.2.3 ignore unrecognized; also contract Parsing rule 4 (marked lane convention).
abc is not delta-seconds (9111 SS1.2.2 1*DIGIT); directive ignored (9111 SS5.2.3); contract rule 4.
-1 is a valid token but not 1*DIGIT (9111 SS1.2.2) -> directive absent; contract rule 4.
RFC 9111 SS4.2.1: "either the first occurrence should be used or the response should be considered stale"; first occurrence (5) yields revalidate at staleness 30.
RFC 9111 SS5.2: "cache directives are identified by a token, to be compared case-insensitively".
RFC 9111 SS1.2.2 overflow -> consider value 2147483648 (note: outcome identical unclamped since 1e9 < raw 99999999999; representability nuance = finding F4).
RFC 5861 SS3 "when present in an HTTP response"; request swr is unrecognized (9111 SS5.2.3 MUST ignore) -> revalidate.
RFC 9111 SS4 reuse list (fresh -> reusable, no response no-cache) + SS4.3.3: on 5xx the cache can act as if the server failed to respond and send the stored response subject to SS4.2.4.
RFC 9111 SS4.2: 0 > 0 false -> stale; no extension permission -> revalidate (9111 SS4.2.4).
Contract Input table (error absent or null when event is request); RFCs silent on the tool I/O mapping.
Contract Input table (error required when event is error).
Contract Input table (integer >= 0); consistent with 9111 SS4.2.3 age construction (non-negative).
Contract Input table (JSON booleans refused; isinstance-bool would otherwise alias int).
Contract Input table (floats refused; delta-seconds and ages are integral).
Contract Parsing rule 2 (no whitespace around =); 9111 SS5.2 ABNF cache-directive = token [ "=" ( token / quoted-string ) ] admits no internal OWS.
Contract Parsing rule 2 (empty value after =); ABNF requires a value production after "=".
Contract Parsing rule 2 (unterminated quote); quoted-string ABNF (9110 SS5.6.4, S478) requires the closing DQUOTE.
Contract rule 5 (request directives max-age/max-stale/min-fresh/only-if-cached declared outside this contract -> refuse); 9111 SS5.2.1.2 defines the directive but the contract's scope excludes it.
Contract Input table (unknown keys -> refuse); tool I/O is contract-defined.
RFC 5861 SS4: 200 not in the enumerated error set -> not-an-error.
Contract Input table (error restricted to 100-599; 99 is not a valid HTTP status).
Contract Input table (string error limited to "network").
RFC 9110 SS5.6.4 quoted-string (comma is qdtext) + SS5.6.1 list split outside quoted-strings (contract rule 1); the swr-looking text is inside foo's value and is not a directive.

Contract Prohibited clause marked convention ("qualified or not - conservative lane convention"); 9111 SS5.2.2.4 qualified form permits field-excluded reuse but the tool cannot express field exclusion.
Contract rule 1 (empty elements skipped); RFC 9110 SS5.6.1 list grammar treats empty elements as non-members (S478 ground).
Inclusive boundary (5861 SS4 "more stale than the indicated amount"): staleness 0 is not more stale than window 0; 9111 SS4.2 equality means stale.
Contract rule 5 (storage directives no-store/private/public ignored; the response is taken as already stored; storage decided elsewhere).
RFC 9110 SS5.6.3 OWS = *( SP / HTAB ) around list elements; contract rule 1 strips SP/HTAB.
Contract Parsing rule 4 (quoted request value -> directive absent, marked lane convention) + Decision rule 4 (fall back to response sie); consistent with 9111 SS5.2.3 + 5861 SS4 response scope.
Contract Input table (shared must be JSON boolean).
Contract Parsing rule 2 (text after closing quote); quoted-string ABNF (9110 SS5.6.4) ends at the closing DQUOTE.
